RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-64107D6EF7-65599
Member: Sawyer Foster (Member ID: W558551284)
Requested Service: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-01
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-28

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01 (Reference # POC-64107D6EF7-65599). The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records from my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD (orthopedic surgery), addresses that stated reason directly and requests that the denial be reversed.

1. The specific policy applied to this request was not identified in the denial notice.

The denial notice states only that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," without naming a specific policy title, number, or version. Based on my own research, Anthem's named clinical guideline for this procedure is "CG-SURG-74 – Total Ankle Replacement," but Anthem's medical-necessity review of this CPT code has been described in Anthem provider communications as delegated to Carelon Medical Benefits Management, Inc. (formerly AIM Specialty Health), whose relevant document is the "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Small Joint Surgery" (Doc ID MSK06-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025). I was not able to independently confirm which specific document and version number was used to review my request. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Anthem identify in writing the exact policy document, section, and version applied to Reference # POC-64107D6EF7-65599, so that I can confirm every applicable criterion has been addressed.

2. To the extent the Carelon Small Joint Surgery guideline's Total Ankle Arthroplasty criteria apply, my documented condition and treatment meet them.

That guideline states that "[t]otal ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL the following criteria are met: Radiographic confirmation of Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 arthritis of the tibiotalar joint OR avascular necrosis of the talus without collapse" (Carelon Medical Benefits Management, "Small Joint Surgery," Doc ID MSK06-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025). My weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-06-05 show "tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts" — findings consistent with advanced tibiotalar arthritis. [The radiology report/surgeon's note in the packet does not state an explicit Kellgren-Lawrence numeric grade; I am asking Dr. Okafor to supply an addendum expressly grading the radiographs on the Kellgren-Lawrence scale, and I request that Anthem hold this appeal open to receive that addendum.]

An earlier version of the same Carelon guideline (archived version effective 11/17/2024) stated that total ankle arthroplasty additionally requires that "[s]ignificant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management." I did not confirm that this exact sentence still appears verbatim in the version effective 11/15/2025, so I am not asserting it as current plan language with certainty — but to the extent a conservative-management requirement of this kind applies, my records show it is satisfied several times over:

- Symptom duration: 18 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Supervised physical therapy: 14 weeks (2026-03-09 through 2026-06-15), 18 completed visits, focused on ankle strengthening and balance, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Medication trial: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- Injection therapy: corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16, providing only 4 weeks of partial relief.

This is more than 3 months of multi-modal, supervised conservative treatment, all of which failed to provide durable relief.

The Carelon guideline also defines the severity threshold for these procedures — in a version I was able to retrieve directly — as: "significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes." I was not able to confirm this exact sentence in the 11/15/2025 version specifically, so I note it here only as an indication of the type of functional documentation the plan has historically required, not as a confirmed current-version quote. My records document exactly this kind of impairment: I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to walking two blocks, and examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side with range of motion limited by pain. [A specific numeric VAS pain score does not appear in the summary provided to me; I am asking Dr. Okafor to document a current VAS pain rating in an addendum, since the guideline language I found ties functional impairment to that specific scale.]

3. General documentation requirements cited by the plan's own guideline are met by the enclosed records.

The same Carelon guideline document (Small Joint Surgery, Doc ID MSK06-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025, retrieved directly) states: "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components: Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented." Enclosed with this appeal are:

- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-09 to 2026-06-15, 18 visits) documenting duration and type of conservative treatment;
- Documentation of the 4-month NSAID trial and the 2026-05-16 corticosteroid injection and its limited, temporary benefit;
- The 2026-06-05 weight-bearing radiograph report showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts;
- Dr. Okafor's clinical notes documenting 18 months of symptom duration, antalgic gait limited to two blocks, and positive provocative testing with pain-limited range of motion.

Taken together, these records supply exactly the categories of information the plan's own documentation standard describes — symptom duration and severity, functional limitation, and type/duration of conservative treatment — and I believe they resolve the "incomplete documentation" basis for denial. If any specific additional item is still considered missing, I am requesting that Anthem identify that item specifically, in writing, rather than issue a general incompleteness finding, so that Dr. Okafor's office can supply it promptly and within the appeal window.

4. Absence of contraindications.

The medical record reflects no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status. I am not aware of, and was not able to independently confirm the exact wording of, the plan's specific list of contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty, but I want the record to reflect that none of these commonly cited concerns (active infection, uncontrolled substance use) are present in my case, and my BMI does not reflect morbid obesity.

Requested Action

I respectfully request that Anthem/Carelon:
1. Identify, in writing, the exact policy or guideline document, section, and version applied to this specific denial;
2. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27702 based on the enclosed documentation; or, in the alternative,
3. Specify precisely what additional documentation is still required to complete the medical-necessity review, so it can be submitted well within the appeal deadline of 2027-01-28.

I have enclosed copies of the physical therapy discharge summary, imaging report, medication/injection records, and my surgeon's clinical notes referenced above. Please contact Dr. Okafor's office at [surgeon's office phone number] or me directly at [phone number]/[email address] if any additional information is needed.

If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to exercise my right to an Independent External Review through the New Hampshire Insurance Department, as provided under New Hampshire law.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Foster
Member ID: W558551284

Enclosures:

- Clinical/exam notes from Dr. Okafor, MD
